summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and prior pulmonary embolism on warfarin was admitted for dyspnea on exertion and right-sided chest pain. He had a desaturation event to the 80s during a primary care visit and was referred to the emergency department. Workup ruled out pulmonary embolism and myocardial infarction with negative CT angiogram, serial troponins, and EKGs. Chest pain was reproducible on palpation, consistent with costochondritis. Initial chest imaging showed findings concerning for pneumonia, but these were attributed to atelectasis given clinical stability and lack of infection markers. His heart failure was stable with low BNP and normal echocardiogram. Hypomagnesemia was identified and corrected. He improved with acetaminophen and ibuprofen, resumed home medications including warfarin (INR 2.5), and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up on magnesium levels and continue all chronic disease management.
